## Summary

The feature required adding `ignore_class` support to the `SparseCategoricalCrossentropy` metric. The underlying loss function `sparse_categorical_crossentropy` already implemented `ignore_class` (it zeroes out ignored samples and attaches a keras mask to its result), so the work was to (1) wire the parameter through the metric and (2) ensure the mask actually excludes samples from the mean's denominator.

### Changes

**`keras/src/metrics/probabilistic_metrics.py`** — `SparseCategoricalCrossentropy`:
- Added `ignore_class=None` to `__init__` (matching the requested signature, positioned before `axis`).
- Forwarded it to the wrapped loss fn via `super().__init__`, stored `self.ignore_class`, and added it to `get_config`.
- Documented the parameter in the docstring.

**`keras/src/metrics/reduction_metrics.py`** — `reduce_to_samplewise_values`:
- When the values carry a keras mask (as set by the loss under `ignore_class`) but no `sample_weight` was supplied, the mask is now converted into a `sample_weight`. Previously the mask was only honored when a `sample_weight` was already present — meaning ignored samples (value 0) were excluded from the numerator but still inflated the count.
